column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|10-10|1930|Χάρολντ Πίντερ|Harold Pinter|Harold Pinter was an English playwright, screenwriter, director and actor. He wrote plays such as "The Homecoming" and "The Caretaker" and in 2005 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 2008.
bio|10-10|1946|Ναότο Καν|Naoto Kan|Naoto Kan is a Japanese politician. He was Prime Minister of Japan from 2010 to 2011 and had to deal with the earthquake and the Fukushima nuclear accident.
bio|10-10|1963|Εντίθ Πιάφ|Édith Piaf|Édith Piaf was a French singer, known as "the little sparrow". She sang hits such as "La vie en rose" and "Non, je ne regrette rien". She died in 1963.

bio|10-10|1985|Όρσον Γουέλς|Orson Welles|Orson Welles was an American director and actor. He directed and starred in "Citizen Kane" in 1941, a film regarded as one of the greatest in history. He died in 1985.

bio|10-11|1531|Ούλριχ Ζβίγγλιος|Ulrich Zwingli|Ulrich Zwingli was a Swiss priest and reformer of Zurich. He led the Swiss Reformation and was killed in 1531 at the Battle of Kappel, in a conflict between Catholics and Protestants.

bio|10-11|1884|Έλινορ Ρούσβελτ|Eleanor Roosevelt|Eleanor Roosevelt was the wife of President Franklin Roosevelt and an activist. She contributed to the drafting of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights of the United Nations. She died in 1962.
bio|10-11|1885|Φρανσουά Μωριάκ|François Mauriac|François Mauriac was a French writer. He wrote "Thérèse Desqueyroux" and in 1952 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1970.

bio|10-11|1889|Τζέιμς Πρέσκοτ Τζάουλ|James Prescott Joule|James Prescott Joule was an English physicist. He studied the relationship between heat and mechanical work, and the unit of energy, the joule, bears his name. He died in 1889.
bio|10-11|1896|Άντον Μπρούκνερ|Anton Bruckner|Anton Bruckner died in 1896 in Vienna. He was an Austrian composer and organist and wrote nine major symphonies and sacred works.

bio|10-11|1937|Μπόμπι Τσάρλτον|Bobby Charlton|Bobby Charlton was an English footballer. He played for Manchester United and was a member of the national team that won the World Cup in 1966. He died in 2023.

bio|10-11|1942|Αμιτάμπ Μπατσάν|Amitabh Bachchan|Amitabh Bachchan is an Indian actor and one of the biggest stars of Bollywood. He has appeared in more than 200 films and also hosts the Indian version of "Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?".
bio|10-11|1963|Ζαν Κοκτώ|Jean Cocteau|Jean Cocteau died in 1963, a few hours after Édith Piaf. He was a French poet, writer and director, with works such as "Beauty and the Beast".
bio|10-11|1992|Cardi B|Cardi B|Cardi B, whose real name is Belcalis Almánzar, is an American rapper. She became known with the song "Bodak Yellow" and has won a Grammy Award.

bio|10-12|1537|Εδουάρδος ΣΤ΄|Edward VI|Edward VI was king of England from 1547. He was the son of Henry VIII and came to the throne as a child. During his reign England became more Protestant. He died young, in 1553, at the age of 15.

bio|10-12|1798|Πέτρος Α΄|Pedro I|Pedro I was the first emperor of Brazil. In 1822 he declared independence from Portugal and abdicated in 1831. As Pedro IV he was also king of Portugal. He died in 1834.
bio|10-12|1870|Ρόμπερτ Λη|Robert E. Lee|Robert E. Lee was an American general. He led the army of the Southern states in the Civil War and surrendered in 1865. He died in 1870.
bio|10-12|1896|Εουτζένιο Μοντάλε|Eugenio Montale|Eugenio Montale was born in Genoa in 1896. He was an Italian poet and in 1975 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1981.
bio|10-12|1924|Ανατόλ Φρανς|Anatole France|Anatole France was a French writer. He wrote "The Crime of Sylvestre Bonnard" and in 1921 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1924.

bio|10-12|1935|Λουτσιάνο Παβαρότι|Luciano Pavarotti|Luciano Pavarotti was born in 1935 in Modena, Italy. He was one of the best-known opera tenors and took part in the "Three Tenors" concerts. He died in 2007.

bio|10-12|1968|Χιου Τζάκμαν|Hugh Jackman|Hugh Jackman is an Australian actor and producer. He became known as Wolverine in the "X-Men" films and starred in "Les Misérables" and "The Greatest Showman".

bio|10-12|1999|Ουίλτ Τσάμπερλεϊν|Wilt Chamberlain|Wilt Chamberlain was an American basketball player. In 1962 he scored 100 points in one NBA game, a record that has not been surpassed. He died in 1999.

bio|10-12|2011|Ντένις Ρίτσι|Dennis Ritchie|Dennis Ritchie died in 2011. He was an American computer scientist who created the C programming language and contributed to the development of the Unix operating system.
bio|10-13|54|Κλαύδιος|Claudius|Claudius was a Roman emperor from 41 to 54. During his reign Rome conquered Britain. He died in 54, after being poisoned, as ancient sources report.
bio|10-27|1605|Ακμπάρ ο Μέγας|Akbar the Great|Akbar the Great was emperor of the Mughal Empire of India from 1556. He expanded the state and followed a policy of religious tolerance. He died in 1605.

bio|10-13|1821|Ρούντολφ Βίρχοβ|Rudolf Virchow|Rudolf Virchow was a German physician and politician. He is regarded as the father of cellular pathology and argued that every cell comes from another cell. He died in 1902.

bio|10-13|1921|Υβ Μοντάν|Yves Montand|Yves Montand was born in Italy and became a French actor and singer. He appeared in the films "Z" and "The Wages of Fear" and sang "Les feuilles mortes". He died in 1991.

bio|10-13|1925|Μάργκαρετ Θάτσερ|Margaret Thatcher|Margaret Thatcher was a British Conservative politician. She was the first woman Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, from 1979 to 1990, and was known as the "Iron Lady". She died in 2013.

bio|10-13|1927|Τουργκούτ Οζάλ|Turgut Özal|Turgut Özal was a Turkish politician and economist. He was Prime Minister of Turkey from 1983 to 1989 and president until his death in 1993. He developed liberal economic policies.
bio|10-13|2016|Πουμιπόν Αντουνιαντέτ|Bhumibol Adulyadej|Bhumibol Adulyadej, or Rama IX, was king of Thailand from 1946. He reigned for 70 years and was very much loved by the people. He died in 2016.

bio|10-13|2016|Ντάριο Φο|Dario Fo|Dario Fo was an Italian playwright, actor and director. He wrote "Accidental Death of an Anarchist" and "Can't Pay? Won't Pay!". In 1997 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|10-14|1890|Ντουάιτ Αϊζενχάουερ|Dwight D. Eisenhower|Dwight D. Eisenhower was the 34th president of the United States, from 1953 to 1961. In the Second World War he was the supreme commander of the Allied forces in Western Europe. He died in 1969.
bio|10-14|1893|Λίλιαν Γκις|Lillian Gish|Lillian Gish was an American actress. She became known in silent films, with films such as "The Birth of a Nation" and "Broken Blossoms". She died in 1993.

bio|10-14|1906|Χάνα Άρεντ|Hannah Arendt|Hannah Arendt was a German-Jewish philosopher. She wrote "The Origins of Totalitarianism" and "Eichmann in Jerusalem", where she spoke of the "banality of evil". She died in 1975.
bio|10-14|1927|Ρότζερ Μουρ|Roger Moore|Roger Moore was an English actor. He played James Bond in seven films, from 1973 to 1985, and starred in the series "The Saint". He died in 2017.

bio|10-14|1930|Μομπούτου Σέσε Σέκο|Mobutu Sese Seko|Mobutu Sese Seko was the leader of Zaire, today's Congo, from 1965 to 1997. He ruled as a dictator and the country experienced great corruption. He died in 1997.

bio|10-14|1944|Έρβιν Ρόμελ|Erwin Rommel|Erwin Rommel was a German field marshal, known as the "Desert Fox" for his operations in North Africa. He was linked to the conspiracy against Hitler and took his own life in 1944 under pressure.

bio|10-14|1977|Μπινγκ Κρόσμπι|Bing Crosby|Bing Crosby was an American singer and actor. He sang "White Christmas", one of the best-selling singles of all time, and won an Oscar for the film "Going My Way". He died in 1977.

bio|10-14|1990|Λέοναρντ Μπερνστάιν|Leonard Bernstein|Leonard Bernstein was an American composer and conductor. He wrote the music for the musical "West Side Story" and conducted the New York Philharmonic. He died in 1990.
bio|10-14|2010|Μπενουά Μάντελμπροτ|Benoit Mandelbrot|Benoit Mandelbrot was a Polish-French mathematician. He founded the geometry of fractals and gave his name to the Mandelbrot set. He died in 2010.
bio|10-15|1814|Μιχαήλ Λέρμοντοφ|Mikhail Lermontov|Mikhail Lermontov was a Russian poet and writer of Romanticism. He wrote "A Hero of Our Time". He was killed in a duel in 1841, at the age of 26.
bio|10-15|1844|Φρίντριχ Νίτσε|Friedrich Nietzsche|Friedrich Nietzsche was born in 1844 in Röcken, Germany. He was a philosopher and philologist and wrote "Thus Spoke Zarathustra". He died in 1900.
bio|10-15|1917|Μάτα Χάρι|Mata Hari|Mata Hari was a Dutch dancer. During the First World War she was accused of spying for the Germans and was executed in France in 1917. The facts are disputed.

bio|10-15|1926|Μισέλ Φουκώ|Michel Foucault|Michel Foucault was born in 1926 in Poitiers. He was a French philosopher who studied the relationship between power and knowledge, with works such as "Discipline and Punish". He died in 1984.

bio|10-15|1931|Αμπντούλ Καλάμ|A. P. J. Abdul Kalam|Abdul Kalam was born in 1931. He was an Indian scientist and politician and president of India from 2002 to 2007. He developed missiles. He died in 2015.

bio|10-15|1946|Χέρμαν Γκαίρινγκ|Hermann Göring|Hermann Göring was a Nazi official in Germany and commander of the Luftwaffe. He was sentenced to death at the Nuremberg trial and took his own life in 1946, shortly before the execution.

bio|10-15|1987|Τομά Σανκάρα|Thomas Sankara|Thomas Sankara was an officer and politician from Burkina Faso. He was president from 1983 until his death and promoted reforms. He was assassinated in 1987, at the age of 37.
bio|10-15|1988|Μεζούτ Εζίλ|Mesut Özil|Mesut Özil is a German former footballer of Turkish origin. He played as a midfielder for Werder Bremen, Real Madrid and Arsenal and won the World Cup in 2014.

bio|10-15|2012|Νορόντομ Σιχανούκ|Norodom Sihanouk|Norodom Sihanouk was king of Cambodia twice. He led the country's independence from France in 1953 and later abdicated in 2004 in favour of his son. He died in 2012.

bio|10-16|1793|Μαρία Αντουανέτα|Marie Antoinette|Marie Antoinette was queen of France as the wife of Louis XVI. She was born in Austria. During the French Revolution she was condemned and executed by guillotine on 16 October 1793.

bio|10-16|1854|Όσκαρ Ουάιλντ|Oscar Wilde|Oscar Wilde was born in Dublin. He was a writer, known for the novel "The Picture of Dorian Gray" and the play "The Importance of Being Earnest". He was imprisoned in 1895. He died in 1900.

bio|10-16|1886|Νταβίντ Μπεν Γκουριόν|David Ben-Gurion|David Ben-Gurion was the first Prime Minister of Israel and a leader in the founding of the state in 1948. He was born in Poland. He died in 1973.

bio|10-16|1888|Ευγένιος Ο'Νηλ|Eugene O'Neill|Eugene O'Neill was an American playwright. He wrote "Long Day's Journey into Night" and in 1936 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1953.
bio|10-16|1908|Ενβέρ Χότζα|Enver Hoxha|Enver Hoxha was an Albanian communist leader. He ruled Albania from 1944 to 1985, and the country was isolated from the rest of the world. He died in 1985.
bio|10-16|1927|Γκύντερ Γκρας|Günter Grass|Günter Grass was a German writer. He wrote the novel "The Tin Drum" and in 1999 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 2015.
bio|10-16|1946|Γιοάχιμ φον Ρίμπεντροπ|Joachim von Ribbentrop|Joachim von Ribbentrop was Hitler's foreign minister. He was sentenced to death at the Nuremberg trial and was hanged on 16 October 1946.

bio|10-16|1946|Βίλχελμ Κάιτελ|Wilhelm Keitel|Wilhelm Keitel was a German field marshal and head of the Supreme Command. He signed Germany's surrender in 1945. He was sentenced at Nuremberg and hanged in 1946.

bio|10-16|1981|Μοσέ Νταγιάν|Moshe Dayan|Moshe Dayan was an Israeli general and politician. He was defence minister during the Six-Day War in 1967 and foreign minister at the time of the Camp David agreement. He died in 1981.

bio|10-17|1428|Αντρέι Ρουμπλιόφ|Andrei Rublev|Andrei Rublev was a Russian icon painter, one of the greatest in Russian art. His work, the icon of the Holy Trinity, is especially well known. The Orthodox Church honours him as a saint. He died around 1428.
bio|10-17|1813|Γκέοργκ Μπύχνερ|Georg Büchner|Georg Büchner was a German playwright and revolutionary. He wrote "Woyzeck" and "Danton's Death". He died young, in 1837, at the age of 23.

bio|10-17|1849|Φρεντερίκ Σοπέν|Frédéric Chopin|Frédéric Chopin was a Polish pianist and composer of Romanticism. He lived in Paris and wrote nocturnes, waltzes and polonaises for piano. He died in 1849 of tuberculosis.

bio|10-17|1887|Γκούσταβ Κίρχοφ|Gustav Kirchhoff|Gustav Kirchhoff was a German physicist. He formulated Kirchhoff's laws for electrical circuits and, together with Bunsen, developed spectroscopy. He died in 1887.
bio|10-17|1915|Άρθουρ Μίλερ|Arthur Miller|Arthur Miller was an American playwright. He wrote the plays "Death of a Salesman" and "The Crucible". He was married to Marilyn Monroe. He died in 2005.
bio|10-17|1918|Ρίτα Χέιγουορθ|Rita Hayworth|Rita Hayworth was an American actress and dancer, one of the great Hollywood stars of the 1940s. She starred in the film "Gilda". She died in 1987.

bio|10-17|1934|Σαντιάγο Ραμόν ι Καχάλ|Santiago Ramón y Cajal|Santiago Ramón y Cajal was a Spanish histologist and neuroscientist. He proved that the nervous system is made up of separate cells and in 1906 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Camillo Golgi.
bio|10-17|1972|Eminem|Eminem|Eminem, whose real name is Marshall Mathers, is an American rapper, producer and actor. He became known with the album "The Marshall Mathers LP" and the film "8 Mile".
bio|10-17|1979|Κίμι Ράικονεν|Kimi Räikkönen|Kimi Räikkönen is a Finnish racing driver. He won the Formula One World Championship in 2007 with Ferrari.
bio|10-18|1859|Ανρί Μπερξόν|Henri Bergson|Henri Bergson was a French philosopher. He wrote about time and duration and in 1927 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1941.

bio|10-18|1871|Τσαρλς Μπάμπατζ|Charles Babbage|Charles Babbage was an English mathematician and engineer. He designed the Analytical Engine, a forerunner of the modern computer, and is regarded as one of the "fathers" of computing. He died in 1871.
bio|10-18|1893|Σαρλ Γκουνώ|Charles Gounod|Charles Gounod was a French composer. He wrote the opera "Faust" and the "Ave Maria", set to Bach's prelude. He died in 1893.

bio|10-18|1926|Τσακ Μπέρι|Chuck Berry|Chuck Berry was an American singer and guitarist and a pioneer of rock and roll. He wrote hits such as "Johnny B. Goode" and "Roll Over Beethoven". He died in 2017.

bio|10-18|1931|Τόμας Έντισον|Thomas Edison|Thomas Edison was an American inventor. He developed the electric incandescent lamp, the phonograph and the film camera, and he held more than 1,000 patents. He died in 1931.
bio|10-18|1955|Χοσέ Ορτέγα ι Γκασέτ|José Ortega y Gasset|José Ortega y Gasset was a Spanish philosopher. He wrote "The Revolt of the Masses" and supported perspectivism. He died in 1955.

bio|10-18|1956|Μαρτίνα Ναβρατίλοβα|Martina Navratilova|Martina Navratilova was born in Czechoslovakia and became an American citizen. She was a tennis player who won 18 Grand Slam singles titles and nine times the Wimbledon championship.
bio|10-18|1960|Ζαν Κλοντ Βαν Νταμ|Jean-Claude Van Damme|Jean-Claude Van Damme is a Belgian actor and martial artist. He became known for action films such as "Bloodsport" and "Universal Soldier".
bio|10-18|1987|Ζακ Έφρον|Zac Efron|Zac Efron is an American actor. He became known for the film "High School Musical" and also appeared in "Hairspray" and "The Greatest Showman".

bio|10-19|1216|Ιωάννης|King John|John, known as John Lackland, was king of England from 1199. He was forced by the barons to sign the Magna Carta in 1215. He died in 1216, during a war with the barons.
bio|10-19|1745|Τζόναθαν Σουίφτ|Jonathan Swift|Jonathan Swift was an Irish writer and clergyman. He wrote "Gulliver's Travels" and "A Modest Proposal". He died in 1745.

bio|10-19|1862|Ωγκύστ Λυμιέρ|Auguste Lumière|Auguste Lumière was a French inventor. Together with his brother Louis he invented cinema and gave the first public screening in 1895 in Paris. He died in 1954.

bio|10-19|1899|Μιγκέλ Άνχελ Αστούριας|Miguel Ángel Asturias|Miguel Ángel Asturias was a Guatemalan writer and diplomat. He wrote "El Señor Presidente" and in 1967 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1974.

bio|10-19|1910|Σουμπραμανιάν Τσαντρασεκάρ|Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar|Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar was born in 1910 in Lahore. He was an astrophysicist and calculated the Chandrasekhar limit. In 1983 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1995.
bio|10-19|1931|Τζον λε Καρέ|John le Carré|John le Carré, whose real name was David Cornwell, was an English writer. He wrote spy novels, such as "The Spy Who Came in from the Cold". He died in 2020.
bio|10-19|1937|Έρνεστ Ράδερφορντ|Ernest Rutherford|Ernest Rutherford died in 1937. He was a New Zealand physicist who discovered the atomic nucleus and is regarded as the "father of nuclear physics".
bio|10-19|1946|Φίλιπ Πούλμαν|Philip Pullman|Philip Pullman is an English writer. He wrote the trilogy "His Dark Materials", which begins with "The Golden Compass".

bio|10-19|2003|Αλίγια Ιζετμπέγκοβιτς|Alija Izetbegović|Alija Izetbegović was a Bosnian politician. He was the first president of Bosnia and Herzegovina, from 1990 to 1996, during the Bosnian War. He died in 2003.
bio|10-20|1854|Αρθούρος Ρεμπώ|Arthur Rimbaud|Arthur Rimbaud was a French poet of Symbolism. He wrote "The Drunken Boat" and "A Season in Hell". He stopped writing at the age of 20. He died in 1891.
bio|10-20|1859|Τζον Ντιούι|John Dewey|John Dewey was an American philosopher and educator. He supported pragmatism and active learning in education. He died in 1952.
bio|10-20|1891|Τζέιμς Τσάντγουικ|James Chadwick|James Chadwick was an English physicist. He discovered the neutron in 1932 and in 1935 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1974.
bio|10-20|1946|Ελφρίντε Γέλινεκ|Elfriede Jelinek|Elfriede Jelinek is an Austrian writer. She wrote the novel "The Piano Teacher" and in 2004 she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
bio|10-20|1964|Χέρμπερτ Χούβερ|Herbert Hoover|Herbert Hoover died in 1964. He was the 31st president of the United States, from 1929 to 1933, during the Great Depression.

bio|10-20|1971|Snoop Dogg|Snoop Dogg|Snoop Dogg, whose real name is Calvin Broadus, is an American rapper and producer from Long Beach, California. He became known with the album "Doggystyle" in 1993.

bio|10-20|1984|Πολ Ντιράκ|Paul Dirac|Paul Dirac died in 1984. He was an English physicist who developed quantum mechanics and predicted the existence of antimatter. In 1933 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|10-20|1994|Μπαρτ Λάνκαστερ|Burt Lancaster|Burt Lancaster was an American actor. He won an Oscar for "Elmer Gantry" and appeared in the films "From Here to Eternity" and "The Leopard". He died in 1994.

bio|10-20|2011|Μουαμάρ αλ Καντάφι|Muammar Gaddafi|Muammar Gaddafi was a Libyan military officer and politician. He ruled Libya from 1969, after a coup, until 2011. He was killed in October 2011 during the civil war.

bio|10-21|1790|Αλφόνς ντε Λαμαρτίν|Alphonse de Lamartine|Alphonse de Lamartine was a French poet and politician of Romanticism. He wrote the "Poetic Meditations" and was foreign minister of the Second Republic in 1848. He died in 1869.

bio|10-21|1805|Οράτιος Νέλσον|Horatio Nelson|Horatio Nelson was a British vice admiral. He defeated the Franco-Spanish fleet at the Battle of Trafalgar on 21 October 1805 and was killed in the battle.
bio|10-21|1833|Άλφρεντ Νόμπελ|Alfred Nobel|Alfred Nobel was a Swedish chemist and industrialist. He invented dynamite and in his will he founded the Nobel Prizes. He died in 1896.

bio|10-21|1929|Ούρσουλα Λε Γκεν|Ursula K. Le Guin|Ursula K. Le Guin was an American writer of science fiction and fantasy. She wrote "The Left Hand of Darkness" and the "Earthsea" series. She died in 2018.

bio|10-21|1931|Άρτουρ Σνίτσλερ|Arthur Schnitzler|Arthur Schnitzler was an Austrian writer and doctor. He wrote the play "La Ronde" and "Dream Story", which inspired the film "Eyes Wide Shut". He died in 1931.
bio|10-21|1949|Μπενιαμίν Νετανιάχου|Benjamin Netanyahu|Benjamin Netanyahu is an Israeli politician. He has served as Prime Minister of Israel in several terms and is the leader of the Likud party.
bio|10-21|1956|Κάρι Φίσερ|Carrie Fisher|Carrie Fisher was an American actress and writer. She became known as Princess Leia in "Star Wars". She died in 2016.
bio|10-21|1969|Τζακ Κέρουακ|Jack Kerouac|Jack Kerouac was an American writer of the Beat Generation. He wrote the novel "On the Road". He died in 1969.
bio|10-21|1984|Φρανσουά Τρυφώ|François Truffaut|François Truffaut was a French director of the "New Wave". He directed the films "The 400 Blows" and "Jules and Jim". He died in 1984.

bio|10-22|741|Κάρολος Μαρτέλος|Charles Martel|Charles Martel was a Frankish leader. In 732 he defeated the Arabs at the Battle of Poitiers and he was the father of Pepin the Short and the grandfather of Charlemagne. He died in 741.
bio|10-22|1130|Τσου Σι|Zhu Xi|Zhu Xi was a Chinese philosopher and scholar of the Song dynasty. He developed Neo-Confucianism, which dominated Chinese thought for centuries. He died in 1200.

bio|10-22|1383|Φερδινάνδος Α΄|Ferdinand I of Portugal|Ferdinand I was king of Portugal from 1367. He fought without success for the throne of Castile and died in 1383 without a male heir, which led to a succession crisis.

bio|10-22|1811|Φραντς Λιστ|Franz Liszt|Franz Liszt was born in 1811 in present-day Austria. He was a Hungarian composer and virtuoso pianist, with works such as the "Hungarian Rhapsodies". He died in 1886.

bio|10-22|1870|Ιβάν Μπούνιν|Ivan Bunin|Ivan Bunin was a Russian writer. He left Russia after the Revolution and in 1933 became the first Russian to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1953.

bio|10-22|1906|Πωλ Σεζάν|Paul Cézanne|Paul Cézanne was a French painter. He was among the pioneers of modern art and influenced Cubism. He painted still lifes and the mountain Sainte-Victoire. He died in 1906.
bio|10-22|1919|Ντόρις Λέσινγκ|Doris Lessing|Doris Lessing was a British writer. She wrote "The Golden Notebook" and in 2007 she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. She died in 2013.

bio|10-22|1943|Κατρίν Ντενέβ|Catherine Deneuve|Catherine Deneuve is a French actress. She became known for the films "The Young Girls of Rochefort" and "Belle de Jour" and is regarded as one of the great names of European cinema.
